text:
maria_sales: FYI — Enterprise POC with BetaCorp hit a flurry of 5xxs during their API stress ramp at ~2026-03-21T14:33Z. They paused demo. Need triage.

liam_support: On standby. Can you share the exact request pattern and model? Any special headers or routing?

maria_sales: They ran a scripted demo: steady 40 RPS, then rapid ramp to 180 RPS over 15s for ~20s, then back to 20 RPS. Route: /v1/chat (model: redwood-xl-2). No special headers. Example: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain..."}]}'```

harper_infra: I dumped the node and autoscaler metrics for that time window. Observed sustained queue growth and repeated 503s from the inference worker pool. Snippets: 
```[2026-03-21T14:33:07Z] WARN worker_pool queue=640 inflight=48 util=91%
[2026-03-21T14:33:10Z] ERROR request=aa9f 503 reason="queue-overflow" queue=1023
[2026-03-21T14:33:12Z] WARN autoscaler state=warming cooldown_until=2026-03-21T14:34:05Z
[2026-03-21T14:33:20Z] ERROR request=bb2e 504 upstream_deadline
```
Queue stayed >800 for ~35s. Autoscaler was still in cooldown from previous ramp.

liam_support: Do they have burstpool or reserved capacity? Any failover toggles?

harper_infra: This org is on trial tenant - no reserved GPUs and burstpool=0. Failover/model-switch disabled by default for demo to avoid behavior surprises.

liam_support: That matches cause. Quick remediation options: A) temporarily attach a small burstpool (e.g., +3 GPUs) and shorten autoscale cooldown; B) enable runtime soft-fallback to rwd-xl-2-quant for latent requests; C) throttle ingress at proxy (rate limit) to smooth ramp. Which can Sales/Customer accept?

maria_sales: Customer prefers no model swap unless necessary. Billing concerns too. They asked that we avoid surprise charges.

harper_infra: If we do temporary burstpool, we can attach it under a capped budget and pre-approve billing for the demo window. That avoids surprise. I'll prepare a short opt-in link.

nora_security: Quick check on quantized variant: it runs in the same VPC region and maintains E2E encryption. Data handling & retention same. If we document it in the questionnaire it should be fine for POC.

liam_support: Operational plan: 1) apply short-term mitigations now: enable capped burstpool + reduce autoscale cooldown from 60s->20s, 2) if latency persists, enable soft-fallback for requests >1500ms, 3) collect traces (X-Trace header) and full error logs for postmortem.

maria_sales: Please make the burstpool opt-in URL and the capped budget details. I'll get sign-off from the customer.

deploy-bot: Created triage ticket TRG-2026-1843056789 "betacorp-poc-5xx-surge". Priority: P2.

harper_infra: Implemented temporary config: burstpool +3 GPUs for tenant (budget cap $150), autoscale cooldown -> 20s, soft-fallback toggle ON for >1500ms. Rolling in 45s. Monitoring dashboards pinned.

tracing-bot: Note: Please ask customer to capture failing X-Trace header; sample header format X-Trace: t-0a1b2c3d4e. We retained traces for 10m for this incident.

liam_support: Root cause (prelim): aggressive demo ramp + no burstpool + conservative cooldown => large queue + backend timeouts -> 5xx.

Action items:
- infra (harper_infra): create a pre-approved demo-burstpool flow with explicit budget caps and UI opt-in.
- sales (maria_sales): add demo-burstpool option to POC checklist and get customer consent before stress runs.
- product (liam_support): add a visible demo-mode toggle that temporarily relaxes cooldowns and/or enables soft-fallbacks for sales demos.
- security (nora_security): add quantized-variant entry to the POC security FAQs.

maria_sales: Thanks team. I'll coordinate with BetaCorp and confirm whether they want the capped burstpool for the resumed demo.
